lines.t: Brinewick sits at the edge of the Hollow Sea, where the last of the salt pans meet the last of the road.
The sun has been dimming since before you were born. Tonight it hangs low and pale, like a coin seen through water.
Your left palm has itched since dusk. Now, as the light fails, something under the skin begins to glow.
Across the path, Elder Maren Salt has stopped raking. She is staring at your hand.
The mud ahead is churned flat and dark. Tusk marks scar every tree trunk at the height of your chest.
Something huge shifts in the wallow. A mound of reeds and clay stands up and becomes a boar the size of a cart.
Its small eyes settle on the glow in your palm. It lowers its head.
The Great Mire Boar sinks into its wallow with a long, wet sigh.
Where its tusk raked the stone, a thread of pale light glows, the same light as your palm, and then fades.
It was guarding something. Or running from it.
Brinewick will want to hear this. Elder Maren is waiting.
